newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Future HK leader Tung, finance boss discuss budget.
newsitem.headline: Future HK leader Tung, finance boss discuss budget.

text.p: Hong Kong's post-colonial leader Tung Chee-hwa met Financial Secretary Donald Tsang on Tuesday and discussed the future of the budget after the territory reverts to China in the middle of next year.
The meeting was Tung's latest move towards forming a government-in-waiting to take over next July 1 after Britain pulls out, ending more than 150 years of colonial rule.

Tsang confirmed he discussed post-handover budget matters with Tung but -- in marked contrast to earlier statements in which he expressed confidence that Tung would let him keep his job -- on Tuesday Tsang kept quiet about his future.
He declined to say whether he would stay on after July 1.
"I wish to continue to serve as a civil servant, as a Financial Secretary. It's known to all. But eventually, it's a decision for Mr Tung," Tsang told reporters after the meeting.
Tung began meeting all principal officials of the government on Monday to determine who stays on and who goes.
This month Tung was chosen as the territory's first Chinese leader, the post-colonial Chief Executive, by a China-controlled committee.
In a move likely to boost confidence among Hong Kong's 6.3 million people, last Saturday Tung asked the popular top civil servant Anson Chan to stay on as Chief Secretary and she agreed.
The key topic in the discussion with Tsang was the 1997-98 transitional budget which straddles Hong Kong's return to Chinese rule in 182 days' time.
"Our discussion revolved around the 1997 budget. I have now more or less finalised my own views on the expenditure side and the revenue side. And I took Mr Tung through them quickly," Tsang said.
Tung has pledged to respect the political neutrality of the territory's civil service.
